newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-ARAVINDA CENTURY STEERS SRI LANKA TO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ARAVINDA CENTURY STEERS SRI LANKA TO FINAL.

text.p: A brilliant hundred from Aravinda de Silva helped Sri Lanka to a 51-run win over Pakistan on Monday and booked their place in the final of the triangular Sharjah Cup cricket tournament.

Sri Lanka's leading runscorer in one-day international cricket put the Pakistan attack to the sword with a scintillating 134 off 131 balls which included 11 fours and four sixes, two each off Waqar Younis and Saqlain Mushtaq.

Aravinda's eighth century in 201 one-day internationals enabled Sri Lanka to recover from the early losses of Romesh Kaluwitharana and Marvan Atapattu, both lbw to Waqar, to post a challenging 251 for seven in the allotted 50 overs.
The man of the match was well supported by Sanath Jayasuriya (67 off 94 balls with seven fours) and the two put on 124 runs for the third wicket.
Pakistan, in reply, failed to build up the momentum against a disciplined Sri Lanka attack, spearheaded by spinners Muttiah Muralitharan and Kumar Dharmasena, who both claimed three wickets each.
Ramiz Raja and Inzamam-ul-Haq raised visions of a fightback but their 77-run stand off 102 balls for the fourth wicket, proved an illusion as both fell to Muralitharan.

Inzamam top-scored for Pakistan with 62 off 66 balls which included five fours and one six. During the course of his innings, Inzamam became the fifth Pakistani batsman to score 4,000 runs in one-day internationals.
Zimbabwe are the third team in the tournament.
